title: Using AI for Root Cause Analysis of Simulation Failures
gist: Tom Anderson, a long-time AMIQ EDA writer, describes a demo of the Root Cause Analysis profile in AMIQ EDA's DVT AI Assistant, in which an AI agent autonomously parses UVM simulation logs, analyzes waveforms and navigates source code to produce an evidence-linked failure report. The capability is also exposed to external agents (Cursor, Claude Code, Codex, Copilot, Kiro) via the AMIQ EDA DVT MCP Server.

insights.claim: AMIQ EDA's DVT AI Assistant Root Cause Analysis profile orchestrates a specialized AI agent that drives the entire simulation-failure debug workflow autonomously from a simple prompt like 'investigate the test failure.'
insights.speaker: Tom Anderson
insights.so_what: Agentic automation is moving into verification debug, one of the most labor-intensive chip design tasks.
insights.locator: At some point during the fifth step

insights.claim: The RCA agent parses raw simulation logs into structured UVM messages, queries waveform signal changes around the failure timestamp, and uses compiler-backed code navigation to reconstruct a timeline of events.
insights.speaker: Tom Anderson
insights.so_what: Structured, compiler-backed tool access is what makes agentic debug reliable versus raw LLM reading of files.
insights.locator: As the demo shows, the agent

insights.claim: The RCA output is a structured report with a chronological, timestamped chain of events linking log messages directly to waveform data, with hyperlinks for cross-correlation.
insights.speaker: Tom Anderson
insights.so_what: Evidence-backed outputs address trust concerns about AI-generated debug conclusions.
insights.locator: The AI agent queries the waveform

insights.claim: Debugging UVM simulation failures is a tedious multi-step process (find error, correlate to source, trace hierarchy, add waveform signals, piece together cause, trial fix) and everything before the 'aha!' moment can be automated by AI, according to Tom Anderson.
insights.speaker: Tom Anderson
insights.so_what: Large share of verification engineer time is addressable by automation, a productivity lever for chip development.
insights.quote: Everything leading up to that can be automated by AI, and that’s what the demo shows.
insights.locator: At some point during the fifth step

insights.claim: AMIQ EDA's RCA capability is included in DVT IDE for VS Code and Eclipse, and external AI agents such as Cursor, Claude Code, Codex, Copilot or Kiro can access it via the AMIQ EDA DVT MCP Server with companion skills.
insights.speaker: Tom Anderson
insights.so_what: EDA vendors are exposing domain tools to general-purpose coding agents via MCP, making them infrastructure for horizontal AI agents.

insights.claim: Some engineers worry GenAI-produced design and verification code will degrade their skills or make jobs boring, but Tom Anderson argues automating routine tasks frees humans for creative work.
insights.speaker: Tom Anderson
insights.so_what: Framing of AI as augmenting rather than replacing verification engineers.

insights.claim: Tom Anderson, who has worked with AMIQ EDA for almost nine years, says nothing he has seen from the company impressed him as much as this AI root-cause-analysis demo.
insights.speaker: Tom Anderson
insights.so_what: Suggests a step-change in EDA AI capability, though from a commercially affiliated writer.
insights.locator: I've been working with AMIQ EDA
